finalText:
I went through all 380 commits and the PR sheet. Out of that, only ~12 things are actually visible to someone installing 4.2 — everything else was dependency bumps, refactors (same "collapse the two retry helpers," "move the config loader," "rename Ctx to RequestCtx" pattern repeated per-module), CI/test churn, or docs. I've written those into `CHANGELOG.md`. Notes on the judgment calls:

- **Breaking**: `fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403` (#4223) changes a status code your users' integrations may branch on — same category as the timeout-units break in 4.1.0, so I filed it there rather than under Fixed.
- **Added**: only one real feature — webhook delivery retries with backoff (#4191).
- **Fixed**: several bug messages recur verbatim across modules (e.g. "guard the null cursor in the paginator" landed separately in queue, API, webhooks, and DB; "drop the duplicate header" landed in core, HTTP, and billing). I collapsed each into one bullet naming all the affected areas rather than listing near-duplicate lines — a reader doesn't care that it was four separate PRs.
- I put the DB request-body logging fix (#4157) near the top since it's a privacy-relevant fix, even though it wasn't the most recent.
- I left out the perf commits (batched metric writes, avoided a clone, skipped a JSON round-trip, reused a parsed schema) — none looked large enough to be user-noticeable, consistent with 4.1.0/4.0.3 not having a Performance section.

One thing worth flagging: the commit log and the PR sheet don't line up 1:1 (127 PR rows vs 380 commits, and a couple of entries have mismatched authors/dates for what looks like the same change, e.g. `#4176`/`be03287`). I used the PR sheet's "code" labels as a sanity check on which fixes were real, but treated `commits.log` as the source of truth. Worth a quick sanity check on your end if that discrepancy matters to you.
